title: priority-lease-oracle: proactive bounded reservations and degradation fence
author: Anya Patel
release_notes: Introduce Priority Lease Oracle for bounded ephemeral reservations; adds per-lease utilization telemetry and a degradation fence to preserve throughput guarantees under high contention. Includes operator docs and console visualization for lease heatmaps.
description: Motivation: Provide a middle-ground between instantaneous burst tokens and long-term reservations so low-latency tenants can opt into short-lived bounded reservations that are proactively reclaimed or hardened into commitments when load patterns justify it. This reduces tail throttling and makes autoscaler decisions more stable in mixed workloads. What this PR does: 1) Implements a Priority Lease Oracle component that issues timeboxed 'leases' with configurable size, priority, and soft-to-hard threshold logic; 2) Adds a degradation fence mechanism that prevents aggressive lease hardening when global headroom is below configured SLO thresholds; 3) Emits new telemetry streams for per-lease utilization, lease churn, and lease-to-commitment conversion rate for downstream costing and alerting; 4) Exposes a concise operator API and console view to visualize active leases and recent conversions. Design summary: The oracle receives lease requests from the admission layer. Each lease is evaluated against a local headroom estimator and a global threshold oracle which linearizes recent utilization and predicted short-term capacity. Leases are granted as bounded credits with an expiry and a softThreshold value. If utilization for a tenant consistently exceeds softThreshold over an observation window and global headroom is sufficient, the oracle upgrades the lease to a short-term commitment (hardening) and notifies the autoscaler and billing pipeline. If global headroom is low, the degradation fence triggers conservative backoff and emits a lease-defer event so clients fall back to pre-configured lower-priority paths. Rollback plan: The controller supports feature-flag gating via config priorityLease.enabled=false. Rolling back sets the gate to false and drains active leases over their TTL. Also a 'revert-lease-oracle' runbook is included in docs. Testing and validation: Unit tests for oracle heuristics and conversion logic; integration test that simulates mixed-tenancy bursts and validates that tail latency stays within SLO and that upgrade/downgrade paths are exercised; e2e canary run on a dedicated pool with synthetic bursts. CI: initial lint and unit failures fixed in subsequent commit; final run green. Observability: New metrics prefixed redwood.leases.{granted,converted,expired,rejected,utilization_p75,utilization_p95}; lease events are exported to eventbus with tags for tenant_id, priority, origin. Console: adds Lease Heatmap panel and a Lease Audit table under Dedicated -> Pools. Backwards compatibility: Leasing is opt-in and does not change default admission behavior. Security: tenant-scoped leases only; audit logs retained for 90 days. Related work: follows ideas from ENG-1429 proactive reservations and borrows telemetry hooks added in ENG-1487. Linear ticket SUP-9087 captured a customer incident where rapid short bursts caused repeated rejections; this PR implements a mitigation path. Checklist: - [x] PriorityLeaseController implementation - [x] Threshold oracle and degradation fence - [x] Telemetry and event exports - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Console panels and docs - [x] Runbook and rollback steps Performance notes: In perf canary, enabling leases at 10% of pool capacity reduced tail 99.9th latency by ~18% for bursty tenants while increasing short-term committed capacity by ~4% during conversion windows. Cost impact: conversions are charged through existing commitment billing path; default lease TTLs are conservative to avoid billing surprises. Operator config: new config section 'priority_lease' with fields max_lease_per_tenant, default_ttl_ms, soft_to_hard_window_ms, degradation_fence_threshold_pct. API surface: POST /pools/{id}/leases to request a lease; GET /pools/{id}/leases for active leases; admin endpoints to adjust thresholds. Docs: added RFC and operator guide under docs/dedicated/priority-leases.md. Known limitations: rare oscillation observed in synthetic workloads with extreme oscillatory load; mitigations included extra hysteresis and a conversion cooldown. Future work: predictive conversion using short-horizon forecasting and economy-aware lease sizing.
commits: 1) add priority lease oracle and controller; 2) add autoscaler hooks for lease->commit conversion; 3) telemetry: lease metrics and eventbus integration; 4) console panels and docs; 5) tests and runbook; 6) fix lint and race in headroom estimator; 7) tweak default thresholds after canary
